info.title: NocoDB v3
info.description:
NocoDB v3 REST API.

## Authentication

Every operation requires authentication. For programmatic access use an API token, sent as either `xc-token: <token>` or `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A request succeeds only if both the token and the owning user's role allow it. See [API tokens](https://docs.nocodb.com/account-settings/api-tokens/).

## Errors

Most errors return `{"error": "<code>", "message": "<text>"}`, plus `details` when there is extra context. Some older paths still answer with a bare `{"msg": "<text>"}` and no `error` code. Match on `error`, not on `message`.

## Conventions

`PATCH` is a merge — omitted properties are left unchanged and an explicit `null` clears a nullable one. Requests are rate limited per user — all API tokens belonging to one user share a quota — and answer `429` with `Retry-After` when throttled. Limits and page sizes are configurable per deployment.

This API endpoint allows you to retrieve records from a specified table. You can customize the response by applying various query parameters for filtering, sorting, and formatting.

**Pagination**: The response is paginated by default, with the first page being returned initially. The response includes the following pagination fields as top-level properties alongside `records`:

- **next**: URL to retrieve the next page of records. For example, `"https://app.nocodb.com/api/v3/tables/medhonywr18cysz/records?page=2"`. Returns `null` when on the last page.
- **prev**: URL to retrieve the previous page of records. Returns `null` when on the first page.
- **nestedNext**: URL to retrieve the current page of records with the next set of nested (linked record) data. Returns `null` when there are no more nested pages.
- **nestedPrev**: URL to retrieve the current page of records with the previous set of nested data. Returns `null` when on the first nested page.

These pagination fields are particularly valuable when working with large datasets divided into multiple pages. They provide the necessary URLs to seamlessly navigate forward and backward through the dataset.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Restricts the response to the listed fields. By default **every** field of the table is returned.

A field may be named by its id or its title. An unknown name is rejected with `422 ERR_FIELD_NOT_FOUND`.

Example: `fields=["field1","field2"]` or `fields=field1,field2`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Allows you to specify the fields by which you want to sort the records in your API response. Accepts either an array of sort objects or a single sort object.

Each sort object must have a 'field' property specifying the field name and a 'direction' property with value 'asc' or 'desc'.

Example: `sort=[{"direction":"asc","field":"field_name"},{"direction":"desc","field":"another_field"}]` or `sort={"direction":"asc","field":"field_name"}`

If `viewId` query parameter is also included, the sort included here will take precedence over any sorting configuration defined in the view.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description:
Enables you to define specific conditions for filtering records in your API response. Multiple conditions can be combined using logical operators such as 'and' and 'or'. Each condition consists of three parts: a field name, a comparison operator, and a value.

Example: `where=(field1,eq,value1)~and(field2,eq,value2)` will filter records where 'field1' is equal to 'value1' AND 'field2' is equal to 'value2'. 

You can also use other comparison operators like 'neq' (not equal), 'gt' (greater than), 'lt' (less than), and more, to create complex filtering rules.

If `viewId` query parameter is also included, then the filters included here will be applied over the filtering configuration defined in the view. 

Please remember to maintain the specified format, for further information on this please see [the documentation](https://nocodb.com/docs/product-docs/developer-resources/rest-apis#v3-where-query-parameter)

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
Page of records to return, 1 by default.

A page past the end of the result set is rejected with `422 ERR_INVALID_OFFSET_VALUE` rather than returning an empty page — including `page=2` on a table with no records.

Example: `page=2` returns the second page.

parameters.name: nestedPage
parameters.description:
Enables you to control the pagination of your nested data (linked records) in API response by specifying the page number you want to retrieve. By default, the first page is returned. If you want to retrieve the next page, you can increment the page number by one.

Example: `page=2` will return the second page of nested data records in the dataset.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Number of records per page. Defaults to 25.

Capped per deployment (1000 by default, 100 on NocoDB Cloud). A request above the ceiling is not rejected — it is silently served at the ceiling.

Example: `pageSize=100` returns at most 100 records per page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Alias for `pageSize`. When both are given, `limit` wins. Note that `pageSize` is the parameter carried into the `next`/`prev` URLs.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of records to skip, as an alternative to `page`. Ignored when `page` is given.

parameters.name: nestedLimit
parameters.description: Maximum number of linked records returned inside each Link or LinkToAnotherRecord field. Defaults to 1000 (`NC_DB_QUERY_LIMIT_LTAR_V3_LIMIT`). A field truncated at this limit is returned without any indication; there is currently no continuation link for nested records.

parameters.name: viewId
parameters.description: ***View Identifier***. Returns the records visible in that view, in its order, and only the fields visible in it — fields hidden in the view are omitted. A `sort` parameter takes precedence over the view's own sort; a `where` parameter is applied in addition to the view's filters. `fields` narrows the selection further.

parameters.name: linksAsLtar
parameters.description: When set to `true`, Links fields will return full linked record data (id and display value) instead of just a count. This makes Links fields behave like LinkToAnotherRecord (LTAR) fields in the response.

parameters.name: fieldIdOnResult
parameters.description: When set to `true`, record fields are keyed by field id instead of field title. Useful when titles may change or are not unique in the caller's model.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity — an unknown field in `fields` or `sort` (`ERR_FIELD_NOT_FOUND`), or a `page` past the end of the result set (`ERR_INVALID_OFFSET_VALUE`).

Unprocessable Entity — more records than the deployment's bulk cap (`ERR_MAX_PAYLOAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`), a value that is not valid for its field's type, or a malformed composite record id. A link id matching no row answers `404`; a property outside `fields` answers `400`; unrecognised keys inside `fields` are ignored.

oneOf.description: Up to 10 records per request by default; the cap is configured per deployment and exceeding it returns 422. Records are created in the order given.

post.description:
Create one or more records. Send a single object or an array; the array length is capped per deployment (10 by default) and a longer request answers `422`.

Link fields accept the related record's id. Attachment fields replace the whole cell, so send any existing files alongside new ones. See [the NocoDB docs](https://docs.nocodb.com) for field value formats.

parameters.description: **View Identifier**. Scopes the write to a view; a view that does not belong to the table is rejected with `422`.

parameters.description: When set to `true`, Links fields in the response carry the linked records instead of a count.

parameters.name: fieldIdOnResult
parameters.description: When set to `true`, record fields are keyed by field id instead of field title. Useful when titles may change or are not unique in the caller's model.

post.description:
Find-or-create records in a single call. If a record matching the merge key exists it is updated, otherwise a new one is inserted.

Unlike the other write operations, upsert also accepts a **display value** in place of a link target object: a bare string or number is resolved against the related table's display value and must match at least one record. A value matching none is rejected with `400`; a value matching more than one resolves to the first match.

The same per-request bulk cap applies as for create and update — 10 records by default, configured per deployment.

Maximum file size is set per deployment (20 MB by default); the number of files a cell may hold is a plan limit. An oversized file answers `400`.

Example: `where=(field1,eq,value1)~and(field2,eq,value2)` will filter records where 'field1' is equal to 'value1' AND 'field2' is equal to 'value2'. 

You can also use other comparison operators like 'neq' (not equal), 'gt' (greater than), 'lt' (less than), and more, to create complex filtering rules.

If `viewId` query parameter is also included, then the filters included here will be applied over the filtering configuration defined in the view.

The response shape follows the relation type of the link field:

- **has-many, many-to-many** — `records`, an array of `{ id, fields }` objects, empty when nothing is linked.
- **belongs-to, one-to-one** — `record`, a single object, or `null` when nothing is linked. There is no `records` key in this case.

The `record` shapes carry `next`, `prev`, `nestedNext` and `nestedPrev`, all `null`; the `records` shape carries `next` and `prev` only.

Example: `sort=[{"direction":"asc","field":"field_name"},{"direction":"desc","field":"another_field"}]` or `sort={"direction":"asc","field":"field_name"}`

FormFieldValidator.description:
One validation rule on a form field. The renderer matches on `type` with no fallback branch, so a type outside this enum is dropped silently — the enum is kept in sync with `nocodb-sdk`'s validation type unions (`src/lib/form.ts`).

Note `required` is NOT a validator type: use the sibling `required` boolean on the field config. Option limiting is not a validator either: use `is_limit_option`.

Custom validators are evaluated by the Enterprise form renderer only.

type.description:
Type of validation to apply. Applicable field types:
- text: `minLength`, `maxLength`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `includes`, `notIncludes`, `regex`
- Email / PhoneNumber / URL: `email`, `businessEmail`, `phoneNumber`, `url`
- numeric: `min`, `max`
- Date / DateTime: `minDate`, `maxDate`
- Time: `minTime`, `maxTime`
- Year: `minYear`, `maxYear`
- MultiSelect / User: `minSelected`, `maxSelected`
- Attachment: `fileTypes`, `fileSize`, `fileCount`

value.description:
Validator parameter. Number for `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`, `minYear`, `maxYear`, `minSelected`, `maxSelected`, `fileCount`, `fileSize` (kilobytes, whatever `unit` says). String for `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `includes`, `notIncludes`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `minTime`, `maxTime`. Array of MIME patterns (`image/*`, `application/pdf`) for `fileTypes`. Omitted for `email`, `businessEmail`, `phoneNumber`, `url`, which are presence toggles, and for `regex`, which reads `regex` instead.

An empty string or explicit null disables the rule.

message.description: Error message shown when the rule fails. Falls back to a generated message.

regex.description: Regular expression pattern. Required when `type` is `regex`, ignored otherwise. Evaluated by the form renderer in the browser only — the submit endpoint does not re-check it, because an author-supplied backtracking pattern would stall the server.

unit.description: `fileSize` only — the unit the limit was authored in. `value` is stored in kilobytes either way; this only controls how the limit is displayed.
